FRIDAY, OCTOBER 16, 2026

Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

6:00 PM – 9:00 PM MDT

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

Mindful Birding Walk at High Plains Environmental Center

9:00 AM – 11:30 AM MDT

High Plains Environmental Center · 2698 Bluestem Willow Dr · Loveland

A mindful birding walk combines traditional birdwatching with mindfulness techniques, focusing on slow-paced, intentional awareness of birds and nature. Observing birds in their natural habitat can be inspiring and relaxing while also offering a variety of health benefits. This way of connecting with nature encourages purposeful curiosity, builds community, and deepens our appreciation for birds and the natural world. Join us at the High Plains Environmental Center to explore mindfulness and birds and learn simple techniques you can take home and practice on your own. We’ll begin in the classroom and then head outside for a guided walk. All abilities and interests are welcome! We'll provide bird books and binoculars. Please dress appropriately for the weather. Registration: Sign-up information will be available in September. We will notify registered participants of any changes due to weather or other circumstances.

MONDAY, OCTOBER 19, 2026

A Sound Healing Journey into the Womb of the Earth for Ecological Self-Restoration

8:00 AM – 9:30 AM MDT

Eben G Fine Park · Boulder

Facilitated by Ayleen Guzman of Mamafaeria Healing Arts At the center of this offering is the understanding that the Earth is not simply the place where we live, but a living spiritual presence that can become a gateway into connection with the Divine, the Divine Mother, God, our ancestors, and ourselves. The womb of the Earth can become a place of return, remembrance, healing, and transformation. We are living through profound and rapidly changing times. Across many Indigenous, African, Native, and spiritual traditions, there are teachings about periods of great transformation in which humanity is called to remember its relationship with the Earth and return to right relationship with one another. Within my own spiritual framework, this is a time when the Earth is calling us to become more sensitive to her presence, her needs, and the wisdom she carries. The intention of this ceremony is to begin cultivating that relationship consciously.

People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

5:30 PM – 7:30 PM MDT

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Caring for families who care for families

10:00 AM – 12:00 PM MDT

Martin Park · 3600 Eastman Ave · Boulder

"It takes a village" ... a common refrain we hear from parents and those supporting families. But what does it take to cultivate this sense of collective care in a village, or to create said village? This event is a meet and greet for families and those feeling called to support families in a deeper way. We will get to know one another, share our dreams, challenges, and needs...and enjoy the time outside while little ones run around the park (with support!). Who knows, you might even meet people you want to start a daycare share with, or another family to try co-living with!

2:00 PM – 3:30 PM MDT

Weaving across time and space, we face the uneven promise of democracy and the possibilities of liberty and justice for all. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. cards.title: People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)
cards.description: The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Richard Williams: Executive Producer Dewi: Director, cinematographer, editor Sarah Ortegon Highwalking: Field director Jason: Cinematographer, finishing editor

cards.title: Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil
cards.description: Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

cards.title: Caring for families who care for families
cards.description: "It takes a village" ... a common refrain we hear from parents and those supporting families. But what does it take to cultivate this sense of collective care in a village, or to create said village? This event is a meet and greet for families and those feeling called to support families in a deeper way. We will get to know one another, share our dreams, challenges, and needs...and enjoy the time outside while little ones run around the park (with support!). Who knows, you might even meet people you want to start a daycare share with, or another family to try co-living with!

FRIDAY, OCTOBER 16, 2026

Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

6:00 PM – 9:00 PM MDT

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

A mindful birding walk combines traditional birdwatching with mindfulness techniques, focusing on slow-paced, intentional awareness of birds and nature. Observing birds in their natural habitat can be inspiring and relaxing while also offering a variety of health benefits. This way of connecting with nature encourages purposeful curiosity, builds community, and deepens our appreciation for birds and the natural world. Join us at the High Plains Environmental Center to explore mindfulness and birds and learn simple techniques you can take home and practice on your own. We’ll begin in the classroom and then head outside for a guided walk. All abilities and interests are welcome! We'll provide bird books and binoculars. Please dress appropriately for the weather. A Sound Healing Journey into the Womb of the Earth for Ecological Self-Restoration

8:00 AM – 9:30 AM MDT

Eben G Fine Park · Boulder

Facilitated by Ayleen Guzman of Mamafaeria Healing Arts At the center of this offering is the understanding that the Earth is not simply the place where we live, but a living spiritual presence that can become a gateway into connection with the Divine, the Divine Mother, God, our ancestors, and ourselves. The womb of the Earth can become a place of return, remembrance, healing, and transformation. We are living through profound and rapidly changing times. Across many Indigenous, African, Native, and spiritual traditions, there are teachings about periods of great transformation in which humanity is called to remember its relationship with the Earth and return to right relationship with one another. Within my own spiritual framework, this is a time when the Earth is calling us to become more sensitive to her presence, her needs, and the wisdom she carries. MONDAY, OCTOBER 19, 2026

People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

5:30 PM – 7:30 PM MDT

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. cards.title: People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)
cards.description: The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. cards.title: Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil
cards.description: Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

This way of connecting with nature encourages purposeful curiosity, builds community, and deepens our appreciation for birds and the natural world. Join us at the High Plains Environmental Center to explore mindfulness and birds and learn simple techniques you can take home and practice on your own. We’ll begin in the classroom and then head outside for a guided walk. All abilities and interests are welcome! We'll provide bird books and binoculars. Please dress appropriately for the weather. cards.title: Short Film Night: On Place & Belonging
cards.description: A curated selection of short, independent films that will explore what shapes our sense of belonging. The films weave in themes of identity, resilience, and our more-than-human kin.

cards.title: A Sound Healing Journey into the Womb of the Earth for Ecological Self-Restoration
cards.description: Facilitated by Ayleen Guzman of Mamafaeria Healing Arts At the center of this offering is the understanding that the Earth is not simply the place where we live, but a living spiritual presence that can become a gateway into connection with the Divine, the Divine Mother, God, our ancestors, and ourselves. The womb of the Earth can become a place of return, remembrance, healing, and transformation. We are living through profound and rapidly changing times. Across many Indigenous, African, Native, and spiritual traditions, there are teachings about periods of great transformation in which humanity is called to remember its relationship with the Earth and return to right relationship with one another. Within my own spiritual framework, this is a time when the Earth is calling us to become more sensitive to her presence, her needs, and the wisdom she carries. The intention of this ceremony is to begin cultivating that relationship consciously.

cards.title: People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)
cards.description: The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Richard Williams: Executive Producer Dewi: Director, cinematographer, editor Sarah Ortegon Highwalking: Field director Jason: Cinematographer, finishing editor

cards.title: COHere Hub-- Time to Hang, Connect & Create
cards.description: Amidst the many events of COHere, the interstitial space at the Coffee Stand is a time to slow down and connect with fellow COHere attendees and reflect on what you are learning. As an optional activity to partake in: the upcycled tapestry that is collectively being made throughout COHere will be present and you can contribute to it by answering one of the 4 questions through the making of a patch: 1) what are you/we grieving? 2) what are you/we decomposing? 3) what are you/we building? 4) what are you/we dreaming?

cards.title: Growing Gardens Volunteer Shift
cards.description: Growing Gardens offers fall volunteer shifts on our Boulder Farm every Tuesday and Friday. It is a wonderful opportunity to learn about regenerative agriculture, connect with a local food system, get your hands in the dirt, and create community with others. Please register in advance at growinggardens.org/volunteer/ There is no prior experience needed to volunteer with Growing Gardens and we provide all necessary equipment and tools. We just ask participants to wear closed-toed shoes, clothing layers, sunscreen or a hat, and to bring a reusable water bottle.

cards.title: Fall Farm Tour and Tea
cards.description: Join us for an end-of-season farm tour of our Jewish-community, educational, sustainable farm. We will tour our greenhouse, educational garden, no-till vegetable donation field, and meet the goats. Hear about our many efforts to build the earth's soil and the earth's people. We'll also make herbal tea straight from the garden.

cards.title: Social Stitchers Meetup x COHere tapestry curation
cards.description: At the Boulder Library each month all ages of community members come together to crochet, knit, mend, embroider, etc. and make use of communal tools provided by the library. At this particular social stitchers gathering, COHere will be inviting folks to contribute to a communal tapestry about Boulder's ecological and communal resilience. Participants will be prompted to make a patch that responds to one of the 4 questions: 1) what are you/we grieving? 2) what are you/we decomposing? 3) what are you/we building 4) and what are you we dreaming? Embroidery and painting will be ways of decorating patches for the tapestry

cards.title: Dinner Table Economics
cards.description: A potluck and community conversation about Ancestral Economic Healing led by Alex Bernat that will take place at the Hawk's Nest, a house that hosts bi-weekly potlucks focused on creativity, community building, storytelling, etc. The Healing Economics conversation will have a focus on the current calls to action being presented by the San Lazaro community right next door! 6-7pm: Gathering and mingling 7-8pm: Conversation about Ancestral Economic Healing

cards.title: Eco-Poetic Writer's Block Jam
cards.description: Join in an eco-poetic exploration this Cohere with one of the best writing communities in town. Writer's Block out of Mi Chantli studio in Boulder is hip, hop, and made for every level and style. Tonight you'll get to write, share, and mingle with some of the best. No experience necessary. Outside the box all day! Your host for this writers Block is Lee Frankel

cards.title: Caring for families who care for families
cards.description: "It takes a village" ... a common refrain we hear from parents and those supporting families. But what does it take to cultivate this sense of collective care in a village, or to create said village? This event is a meet and greet for families and those feeling called to support families in a deeper way. We will get to know one another, share our dreams, challenges, and needs...and enjoy the time outside while little ones run around the park (with support!). Who knows, you might even meet people you want to start a daycare share with, or another family to try co-living with!

Community Song Circle
cards.description: Join us for a community song circle that will uplift songs about our land, water and resilience. No singing experience or expertise required. All ages welcome.

cards.title: Uprooting Qahr! Power, Privilege, and Paperwork
cards.description: Through monologues, film, and live music, Uprooting Qahr! Power, Privilege, and Paperwork, follows Taishya Adams - educator, artist, and policymaker - as she shares personal and political narratives that confront the colonial cancer that spread from Europe to Africa, the Americas and West Asia. Weaving across time and space, we face the uneven promise of democracy and the possibilities of liberty and justice for all.
